calls.head: The Flames will outshoot the Canucks
calls.body: On shot volume, Calgary is around the middle of the league and Vancouver is one of the league’s worst. That’s about as far apart as two teams get.
calls.call: The Flames take more 5-on-5 shot attempts per 60 than the Canucks.
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 1 and 2 games this season
calls.happened: On 5-on-5 shot attempts per 60, Calgary had 80.7 per 60 and Vancouver 58.0 per 60. Coming in, Calgary was at 58.8 per 60 and Vancouver at 48.6 per 60.

calls.head: Good looks against hopeful ones
calls.body: The Canucks are around the middle of the league for shot quality, at the dangerous end; the Flames are one of the league’s worst, at the hopeful end. Expect that gap to show.
calls.call: The Canucks’ shots are more dangerous on average than the Flames’.
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 1 and 2 games this season
calls.happened: On how dangerous the average shot was, Vancouver had 6.7% a shot and Calgary 4.1% a shot. Coming in, Vancouver was at 6.3% a shot and Calgary at 5.9% a shot.
calls.usual: VAN 6.3% a shot · CGY 5.9% a shot
calls.tonight: VAN 6.7% a shot · CGY 4.1% a shot
calls.beyond: Calgary’s shots at 5-on-5 were less dangerous than usual: a 4.1% chance of scoring on the average shot, against their usual 5.9% (league average 6.3%). A team strays this far about once every 15 games.

VAN.head: We had this close to even (56% for Vancouver), and Vancouver came through.

CGY.head: We had this close to even (44% for Calgary), and it went Vancouver’s way.

surprises.head: Vancouver brought the hits
surprises.body: Vancouver’s hit score in the close stretches of the game was 160, against their usual 82 (100 is league average, adjusted for the arena’s scorer). A team strays this far about once every 60 games.

surprises.head: Vancouver tried a different line
surprises.body: E. Pettersson, L. Karlsson, M. Rossi played 10:30 together at 5-on-5, a trio that isn’t one of Vancouver’s usual lines.

story.head: The Canucks beat the Flames
paras: Matt Coronato opened the scoring late in the first. Four different Canucks scored.

The chances were closer than the score. By our Swing measure, Liam Ohgren had the best night of anyone. The Canucks tried a line they hadn’t used before: Elias Pettersson, Linus Karlsson and Marco Rossi, and it had a hand in three of their goals.

items.text: Whether the Canucks keep that line together at home against Vegas on Sunday.
Both of the preview’s calls held.
